best: Found the single choke point (the LLM singleton's shared AsyncOpenAI client) and wrapped it once, so all five Chat Completions call sites route — the check confirms 5/5 verified, 0 unverified, and the live run proves /v1/responses works for both an OpenAI id and a Claude id with tool calls and usage intact; the unlock_hosts rule is the right narrow shape (configured host only, loopback and *.local deliberately never unlocked so a self-hosted Ollama serving a catalog id like gpt-oss-120b does not leave the box).

Caught the one genuine silent behaviour loss the migration would have caused: MULTIMODAL_MODELS is a hand-written 2024 list containing exactly one catalog id, so any move to a Router model id would have had format_messages strip every browser-agent screenshot and ask_with_images raise before sending. Fixed it by reading image capability from the vendored catalog, with tests, and was honest that image tokens now count toward max_input_tokens.

Read the failure-handling and accounting code rather than just the call sites: spotted that the tenacity decorator retries retry_if_exception_type((OpenAIError, Exception, ValueError)) — i.e. everything, including TokenLimitExceeded and the empty-response ValueError — six times re-billing a growing prompt (18 provider attempts for one ask() in the sim), and that the streaming paths estimate tokens with cl100k_base for Claude ids while TokenLimitExceeded is load-bearing. Both are real defects in this repo, correctly placed as Router-fallback and real-usage work.
misses: Left the thing that actually turns routing on unbuilt. The engineer already shipped a router.policy.json branch, and nd1 names model_map as the mechanism — adding a model_map (claude-3-7-sonnet-* → claude-sonnet-4-6, which they themselves recommend as price-equal and temperature-honouring) plus the [llm.vision] id would have moved real traffic behind one reviewable, revertible line, with the old ids still resolvable. As shipped, every production deployment stays 100% on the vendor; routing is proven only for ids nobody has configured.

No attack on the dominant cost driver, which is the transcript itself, not the per-token price. The agent loop resends the full system prompt plus whole history every step and already has max_input_tokens machinery; history compaction/truncation, trimming duplicated tool schemas, and cache-aware message ordering (stable prefix first, so prompt_cache_key actually hits) would compound with i1 rather than being replaced by it. Relatedly, no latency/tier analysis: every call is labelled user_waiting with no examination of which ones aren't — plan updates and the final summary in planning.py are background bookkeeping and are the obvious Flex-tier candidates, yet Flex appears only as a number borrowed from the lever sheet.

Thin live verification of exactly the paths most likely to break. Two buffered requests were run live; neither streaming path, no vision/image request, and nothing on the catalog-vision branch — which is the only improvement that changes what gets sent to the provider. An expert would have put one real base64 screenshot through ask_with_images on a catalog Claude id live, and one streamed ask_tool, before claiming the capability is restored. The breadth of unlock_hosts also deserved a rail: any configured host (including resellers like PPIO/Jiekou whose whole value is sub-list pricing) silently re-provisions and re-bills catalog ids through Router — disclosed in m2's loses, but an allowlist or per-deployment opt-in would be the safe default rather than a prose warning.
wrong: i1's tests evidence claims "pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/sandbox on the branch: 7 passed"; the check reports 4 passed on router-migrate/improve/policy-cache-timeout — the branch is cut from base and does not carry the migration's three new tests. The number is overstated and suggests the policy branch was validated on top of the wrap when it wasn't.

i1 leads with "-90%, $0.00106 instead of $0.0104" on a 10,362-token prompt. That is a ROUTER.md measurement on someone else's prompt, carried over as this item's headline gain; the price evidence does admit it was not re-measured here, but the figure is presented as the expected result for OpenManus. The real saving depends on this app's prefix stability across steps, which was never measured.

i5's "95% less" for planning and summarising is a list-price ratio, not a measured saving, and ignores that a weaker planner can burn more agent steps — the item's own loses says so, which makes the headline number misleading rather than wrong. Same for "a 40-step browser run": the step count is illustrative but reads as observed.

Both new test files write config/config.toml into the working tree at import time and unlink it afterwards. It passes, but it is import-time mutation of a real config path inside the repo; a fixture or monkeypatched loader is the correct form, and the current shape can interact badly with any test that loads app.config first.

m1's "keeps per-request provider fallback if Router refuses before generating" is asserted with no configuration behind it — no fallbacks are set anywhere in the shipped policy (i3, which would add them, is explicitly not built), so as merged there is no fallback behaviour to keep.
